$comment: Generated by `npm run catalog` from src/core/rules/registry.ts. Do not edit by hand. Descriptions are SCA's own words.

rules.title: Division by zero
rules.summary: A division or remainder whose divisor can be 0.
rules.rationale: Dividing an integer by 0 is undefined behavior: most targets trap, some return garbage.
rules.fix: Check the divisor before dividing, or make sure every caller passes a non-zero value.

rules.title: Null pointer dereference
rules.summary: A pointer that can be NULL is dereferenced (*p, p->f, p[i]).
rules.rationale: Reading or writing through NULL is undefined behavior; on a microcontroller it may silently touch address 0.
rules.fix: Test the pointer before use, or guarantee it can never be NULL at this point.

rules.title: Read of an uninitialized variable
rules.summary: A local variable is read before it is set on some path.
rules.rationale: An uninitialized local holds whatever was on the stack, so the result changes from run to run.
rules.fix: Initialize the variable at its declaration, or set it on every path before it is read.

rules.title: Array index out of bounds
rules.summary: An array is indexed outside its size, or memcpy / memset / memmove writes past its end.
rules.rationale: Accessing past the end of an array corrupts neighboring data or reads garbage; it is undefined behavior.
rules.fix: Check the index against the array size before the access.

rules.title: Signed integer overflow
rules.summary: Signed arithmetic gives a result outside its type, or a cast to a narrower signed type does not fit.
rules.rationale: Signed overflow is undefined behavior; compilers may optimize on the assumption that it never happens.
rules.fix: Check the operands before the operation, or compute in a wider type and range-check the result.

rules.title: Unsigned wrap-around
rules.summary: An unsigned counter is stepped past 0 or past its maximum and wraps around.
rules.rationale: Unsigned arithmetic wraps silently; a counter that goes below 0 becomes a huge number.
rules.fix: Test the value before stepping it.

rules.title: Invalid shift amount
rules.summary: A shift by a negative amount, or by the bit width of the type or more.
rules.rationale: Such shifts are undefined behavior; different CPUs give different results.
rules.fix: Keep the shift amount between 0 and the bit width minus one.

rules.title: Negative value converted to unsigned
rules.summary: A value that can be negative is cast to an unsigned type.
rules.rationale: The cast turns -1 into the largest unsigned value, which then passes range checks it should fail.
rules.fix: Check that the value is not negative before the cast.

rules.title: Dead code
rules.summary: A branch that is never taken, or code that can never be reached.
rules.rationale: Dead code is untested by definition and often shows that a condition is not what the author meant.
rules.fix: Fix the condition, or remove the code that cannot run.

rules.title: Endless loop
rules.summary: A loop whose condition is always true, or a wait loop with no way out.
rules.rationale: A loop that never ends hangs the task; in a wait loop a hardware fault becomes a lock-up.
rules.fix: Add a timeout or an exit condition that can become true.

rules.title: Address of a local returned
rules.summary: A function returns the address of one of its local variables.
rules.rationale: The local's memory is reused after the function returns, so the pointer points to garbage.
rules.fix: Return the value, use a static or caller-provided buffer instead.

rules.title: Memory leak
rules.summary: The function returns (or ends) while it still owns memory it allocated, and no pointer to it is kept.
rules.rationale: The memory can never be freed again. In a long-running program each leak shrinks the heap until an allocation fails.
rules.fix: Free the memory on every path that does not hand it on, or store it where it is freed later.

rules.title: Double free
rules.summary: free() is called on memory that was already freed.
rules.rationale: Freeing twice corrupts the heap's bookkeeping; later allocations can return memory that is still in use.
rules.fix: Set the pointer to NULL right after free() (free(NULL) does nothing), or make sure only one owner frees it.

rules.title: Use after free
rules.summary: Memory is read or written through a pointer after it was freed.
rules.rationale: Freed memory belongs to the allocator again: it may already hold other data, so the read gives garbage and the write corrupts it.
rules.fix: Copy what you still need before free(), and free the memory last.

rules.title: Free of memory not from malloc
rules.summary: free() is called on an array, the address of a variable or a string literal.
rules.rationale: free() only accepts pointers that malloc(), calloc() or realloc() returned; anything else corrupts the heap.
rules.fix: Only free what was allocated; static and local objects need no free().

rules.title: Dangling pointer to a local array
rules.summary: A pointer to a local array is used after the block that declares the array has ended.
rules.rationale: The array's memory is reused once its block ends, so the pointer reads whatever is there now.
rules.fix: Declare the array in the outer block, or make it static.

rules.title: Allocation result not checked
rules.summary: The result of malloc(), calloc() or realloc() is used without testing it against NULL.
rules.rationale: Allocations fail when memory runs out; the NULL result is then dereferenced.
rules.fix: Test the pointer before the first use and handle the failure.

rules.title: Allocation size not in elements
rules.summary: malloc(n) is stored as a pointer to values wider than a byte, but n is not multiplied by the element size.
rules.rationale: malloc() counts bytes. Allocating n bytes for n 16-bit values gives half the memory, and writing the last values overflows the block.
rules.fix: Multiply the count by sizeof the element: malloc(n * sizeof(*p)).

rules.title: sizeof of a pointer used as a buffer size
rules.summary: sizeof(p) of a pointer p is used as the size of the memory p points to (memset, memcpy, malloc, ...).
rules.rationale: sizeof(p) is the size of the pointer itself (4 or 8 bytes), not of the table or buffer, so only part of it is cleared or copied.
rules.fix: Use the object's size: sizeof(*p) times the element count, or sizeof of the array itself.

rules.title: Pointer arithmetic out of bounds
rules.summary: Adding to (or subtracting from) a pointer into an array gives a pointer before its start or more than one past its end.
rules.rationale: Such a pointer is undefined behavior even before it is dereferenced, and any use of it reads or writes outside the array.
rules.fix: Check the offset against the array length before computing the pointer.

rules.title: Missing return value
rules.summary: A function that returns a value can reach the end of its body without a return statement.
rules.rationale: The caller then uses whatever happens to be in the return register: undefined behavior that often looks like a random value.
rules.fix: Return a value on every path, for example a safe default after a switch.

rules.title: Invalid enum value
rules.summary: An integer is cast to an enum type, but its value can be outside the range of the enum's constants.
rules.rationale: Code that switches on the enum assumes one of its constants; an out-of-range value takes a path nobody planned for.
rules.fix: Check the integer against the enum's range before the cast, and map bad values to a safe constant.

rules.title: Call to a function that never returns
rules.summary: A function of the file can never return (an endless loop, or every path stops the program), but it is not declared _Noreturn.
rules.rationale: Readers and tools expect the code after the call to run. A hidden endless loop also hangs the program in a way that is easy to miss (for example until a watchdog reset).
rules.fix: Declare the function _Noreturn (or with a noreturn attribute) when that is intended; otherwise give it a way out.

rules.title: Call through a function pointer made from data
rules.summary: A function pointer is made by casting the address of a data object (an array, a variable) and then called.
rules.rationale: Data memory does not hold code for this function; the call jumps into the data, which crashes or runs garbage (and is often blocked by the memory protection).
rules.fix: Point the function pointer to a real function. Calling code at a fixed address (a boot loader) should use that address as a constant, with a justification.

rules.title: Floating-point equality
rules.summary: Floating-point values are compared with == or !=.
rules.rationale: Rounding makes two computations of the same value differ in the last bits, so exact equality is rarely true when it should be.
rules.fix: Compare the difference with a tolerance: fabsf(a - b) < EPS.

rules.title: Assignment in a condition
rules.summary: An assignment inside the condition of if, while, for or ?:.
rules.rationale: It is easy to read as a comparison, and = typed instead of == is a classic bug.
rules.fix: Assign first, then test the variable in the condition.

rules.title: Assignment used as a value
rules.summary: The result of an assignment is used inside a larger expression (a = b = 0, f(x = 3)).
rules.rationale: Hidden assignments make an expression do two things at once and hide where a variable changes.
rules.fix: Write each assignment as its own statement.

rules.title: Side effect in the right operand of && or ||
rules.summary: ++, -- or an assignment in the right operand of && or ||.
rules.rationale: The right operand only runs when the left one does not decide the result, so the side effect happens only sometimes.
rules.fix: Move the side effect out of the condition.

rules.title: Increment or decrement inside an expression
rules.summary: ++ or -- is part of a larger expression (a[i++] = x).
rules.rationale: Mixing the change of a variable with its use makes the order of effects hard to see and easy to get wrong.
rules.fix: Do the increment or decrement as its own statement.

rules.title: Comma operator
rules.summary: The comma operator is used outside a for header.
rules.rationale: It packs several actions into one expression and is often a typo for a semicolon or a parameter list.
rules.fix: Write the expressions as separate statements.

rules.title: Unclear operator precedence
rules.summary: Bitwise operators mixed with comparisons, shifts or arithmetic, or && mixed with ||, without parentheses.
rules.rationale: C's precedence for these operators surprises people: a & b == c tests b == c first.
rules.fix: Add parentheses that show the intended grouping.

rules.title: Side effect inside sizeof
rules.summary: sizeof is applied to an expression with ++, --, an assignment or a call.
rules.rationale: sizeof does not evaluate its operand, so the side effect never happens.
rules.fix: Do the side effect separately and apply sizeof to a plain expression or a type.

rules.title: switch without default
rules.summary: A switch statement has no default clause.
rules.rationale: Values that no case expects then pass silently; a default clause handles them on purpose.
rules.fix: Add a default clause that handles (or reports) unexpected values.

rules.title: goto
rules.summary: A goto statement is used.
rules.rationale: Jumps make control flow hard to follow, review and analyze.
rules.fix: Restructure with if, loops or an early return.

rules.title: switch fall-through
rules.summary: A case with statements does not end with break, return, continue or goto, so it falls into the next case.
rules.rationale: A forgotten break is a common bug; intended fall-through should be visible.
rules.fix: Add the missing break, or mark intended fall-through with a /* fallthrough */ comment.

rules.title: Body without braces
rules.summary: The body of if, else, for, while or do is not a { } block.
rules.rationale: A line added later looks like part of the body but is not.
rules.fix: Put the body in braces.

rules.title: Empty body (stray semicolon)
rules.summary: if, else, for or while has a lone ; as its body.
rules.rationale: Usually a stray semicolon: the code below then runs every time.
rules.fix: Remove the semicolon; if an empty body is intended, write { } with a comment.

rules.title: else if chain without final else
rules.summary: An if ... else if chain ends without an else.
rules.rationale: Like a switch without default: the remaining cases are not handled on purpose.
rules.fix: Add a final else that handles the rest, or says in a comment why nothing is needed.

rules.title: Floating-point loop counter
rules.summary: A for loop counts with a floating-point variable.
rules.rationale: Rounding makes the number of iterations hard to predict.
rules.fix: Count with an integer and compute the floating-point value from it.

rules.title: Loop counter changed in the body
rules.summary: The counter of a for loop is also changed inside the loop body.
rules.rationale: Readers expect the for header to say how the loop steps; a second change hides that.
rules.fix: Change the counter only in the header, or use a while loop.

rules.title: switch with fewer than two clauses
rules.summary: A switch has no clause or only one.
rules.rationale: An if statement says the same more clearly.
rules.fix: Replace the switch with an if.

rules.title: switch on a boolean
rules.summary: A switch tests a boolean expression (a comparison or a bool variable).
rules.rationale: A boolean has two values; if / else is the natural way to write that.
rules.fix: Use if / else.

rules.title: Condition that never changes
rules.summary: An if condition is always true or always false (e.g. a u8 compared with 255).
rules.rationale: The test is useless, and usually means the author expected another type or value.
rules.fix: Fix the condition or remove it.

rules.title: Recursion
rules.summary: A function calls itself, directly or through other functions of the same file.
rules.rationale: Stack use then depends on the input and cannot be bounded when the code is built.
rules.fix: Rewrite the algorithm as a loop.

rules.title: Octal constant
rules.summary: An integer constant is written in octal (a leading 0, as in 010).
rules.rationale: 010 is eight, not ten; a leading zero is easy to add by accident.
rules.fix: Write the number in decimal or hex.

rules.title: Lowercase l suffix
rules.summary: A literal suffix uses a lowercase l (10l).
rules.rationale: A lowercase l looks like the digit 1.
rules.fix: Write the suffix as L (10L, 10UL).

rules.title: Unsigned constant without U
rules.summary: A hex or octal constant above the signed int range has no U suffix.
rules.rationale: Such a constant silently gets an unsigned type, which changes how comparisons and arithmetic behave.
rules.fix: Add a U suffix so the type is visible.

rules.title: Implicit narrowing or sign change
rules.summary: An assignment, initialization or return converts a value to a narrower type, or between signed and unsigned, without a cast.
rules.rationale: High bits are cut off or the sign changes without anything in the code showing it.
rules.fix: Check the range, then convert with an explicit cast.

rules.title: Signed / unsigned comparison
rules.summary: A comparison where a signed value is converted to unsigned.
rules.rationale: The conversion turns a negative value into a huge one, so -1 < 1U is false.
rules.fix: Check that the signed value is not negative, then cast it.

rules.title: Bitwise operation on a signed value
rules.summary: &, |, ^, ~, << or >> is applied to a signed value.
rules.rationale: Shifting negative values is undefined or compiler-specific, and bit patterns of signed values depend on their representation.
rules.fix: Do bit operations on unsigned types.

rules.title: Variable-length array
rules.summary: An array whose size is only known at run time.
rules.rationale: Stack use then depends on the input and cannot be bounded; a large size overflows the stack without warning.
rules.fix: Use a fixed maximum size and check the length against it.

rules.title: Bit-field with plain int
rules.summary: A bit-field is declared with plain int, char, short or long.
rules.rationale: Whether such a bit-field is signed depends on the compiler.
rules.fix: Declare it with an explicitly unsigned (or signed) type.

rules.title: Integer division stored as float
rules.summary: The result of an integer division is stored as a floating-point value.
rules.rationale: The division is done in integers first, so the fraction is lost before the conversion.
rules.fix: Cast an operand to float so the division is done in floating point.

rules.title: Unused local variable
rules.summary: A local variable is declared but never used.
rules.rationale: Unused variables are noise, and often a sign that the code does not do what was planned.
rules.fix: Remove the variable, or use it as intended.

rules.title: Unused parameter
rules.summary: A function parameter is never used.
rules.rationale: Either the function ignores input it should use, or the parameter is not needed.
rules.fix: Use the parameter, remove it, or write (void)name; when an interface requires it.

rules.title: Name hides an outer name
rules.summary: A local variable has the same name as a parameter, an outer local or a file-level object.
rules.rationale: Readers (and later edits) easily mix up the two variables.
rules.fix: Rename the inner variable.

rules.title: Data shared with an interrupt is not volatile
rules.summary: A file-level object is used by an interrupt handler and by other code, but is not declared volatile.
rules.rationale: Without volatile the compiler may keep the value in a register and never see the interrupt's change.
rules.fix: Declare the object volatile, and protect read-modify-write sequences against the interrupt.

rules.title: External name without a header declaration
rules.summary: A file-level function or object is visible to other files, but no included header declares it.
rules.rationale: Either it is only used in this file (then it should be static) or other files declare it themselves, which lets declarations drift apart.
rules.fix: Make it static, or declare it in the module's header and include that header.

rules.title: Dynamic memory
rules.summary: malloc, calloc, realloc or free (or new / delete) is used.
rules.rationale: Heap use can fail or fragment at run time, so memory use is not known when the code is built.
rules.fix: Allocate statically (fixed-size arrays or pools).

rules.title: Magic number
rules.summary: A numeric constant other than 0 or 1 appears in code without a name.
rules.rationale: A name says what the number means and keeps every use in step when it changes.
rules.fix: Give the number a name with #define, an enum or a const object.

rules.title: Empty parameter list in C
rules.summary: A C function is declared with () instead of (void).
rules.rationale: In C, () means "unknown arguments", so calls with wrong arguments are not checked.
rules.fix: Write (void).

rules.title: Return value ignored
rules.summary: The value a function returns (a status, a count, a flag) is thrown away.
rules.rationale: Errors reported through the return value then go unnoticed.
rules.fix: Check the value, or write (void)f(...); when ignoring it is intended.

rules.title: Cyclomatic complexity
rules.summary: The number of decisions in a function plus one (if, loops, case, &&, ||, ?:) is above the limit.
rules.rationale: Each decision adds a path to understand and to test; complex functions hide bugs.
rules.fix: Split the function into smaller ones, or simplify the logic (tables, early returns).

rules.title: Nesting depth
rules.summary: Control statements are nested deeper than the limit.
rules.rationale: Deep nesting is hard to read and usually means the function does too much.
rules.fix: Return early, or move inner blocks into functions.

rules.title: Function length
rules.summary: A function has more statements than the limit.
rules.rationale: Long functions are hard to review and to test completely.
rules.fix: Split the function by task.

rules.title: Number of parameters
rules.summary: A function has more parameters than the limit.
rules.rationale: Many parameters are easy to mix up and suggest the function has too many jobs.
rules.fix: Group related parameters in a struct, or split the function.

rules.title: Number of return points
rules.summary: A function has more return points than the limit.
rules.rationale: Several exits make it harder to see that every path cleans up and sets its results.
rules.fix: Use one exit at the end, or raise the limit if early returns are your style.

rules.title: Number of called functions
rules.summary: A function calls more different functions than the limit.
rules.rationale: Many dependencies make a function hard to understand and to test in isolation.
rules.fix: Move groups of calls into helper functions.

rules.title: Comment density
rules.summary: A file has fewer comment lines per code line than the limit.
rules.rationale: Code without comments says what it does, but not why.
rules.fix: Add comments that explain intent, units and limits.
